nodes.label: Operational period plan, activate, and close
nodes.rationale: Each OP has its own DataSync that field users subscribe to. Planning must build the next IAP, order resources, and publish assignments while the current period is still worked, without the field seeing the next period, and teams may still debrief into the current period after the next one starts. Plan OP n creates the DataSync on management channels only (status planning), stores field and management channels as plannedChannels, and allows only one planning OP. Activate applies those channels (status open) and publishes the IPP; the previous OP stays open. Close is always a separate manual action with inline confirmation that removes field channels, never a side effect of activation, because someone must decide when a period ends (Paul, 2026-10-11). Open now still opens an OP to the field immediately. Clues, field logs, and the IPP go to currentOpPeriod, which never returns a planning OP. Work on chooses which OP the assignments, roster, and IPP controls apply to. If management channels cannot be read from the MGMT DataSync, planning refuses rather than risk a field-visible OP.

nodes.label: Verified mission group changes
nodes.rationale: TAK changes a mission's groups only when the caller is the mission owner (MISSION_OWNER via the MissionAuthorization token, or an admin), is a member of every group being assigned, and sends allowGroupChange=true. Otherwise it can still return 200 and leave the groups unchanged. Every channel change is verified against the groups TAK reports back; a mismatch is an error and the OP status does not change.

nodes.label: OP owner token
nodes.rationale: The owner token is captured at create and kept in the registry. Channel changes address the mission by guid, so CloudTAK falls back to the caller's stored subscription token when no owner token was saved. OPs created before the 2026-10-11 fix have none, because node-tak dropped the create token when keywords were set at create. The plugin works around that by setting keywords after create; a node-tak fix to keep the token should go upstream. If the fallback token lacks owner rights, the change fails explicitly and a TAK admin must change the channels.

nodes.label: Auto-close OP on activation
nodes.rationale: Rejected (Paul, 2026-10-11): someone must decide when a period ends, and teams returning from the last shift still debrief into the current OP after the next one starts.

nodes.label: Open every OP at creation
nodes.rationale: Previous behaviour. Rejected because the next period's plan, assignments, and IAP would be visible to the field before the period starts.

nodes.label: Trust TAK HTTP 200 for group changes
nodes.rationale: Rejected because TAK silently ignored group changes made without owner rights, which left OPs open to the field after Close without any error.
